failure_analysis.what: Median primary 0.869 (runs 0.878, 0.869, 0.675) vs baseline 0.898; correctness 1 in all runs. cur_median_mb_s 496.93 / 481.84 / 374.28 vs ref ~555-569.
failure_analysis.why: The skip loop only touches the ~25% of bytes outside strings, and many of those are structural (" { } [ ] \n) or on content-free line prefixes, so few bytes are actually skipped while every outside-string byte now pays an extra lineHasContent + OCLS table check before the switch. Net effect is neutral-to-slightly-negative, consistent with the plan's own estimate (~0%). Run 3 is likely contaminated by machine contention: its first ~43 ratios cluster at ~0.62-0.70 and then jump to ~0.85-0.93, a bimodal pattern typical of external load rather than the code change. Excluding it, runs 1-2 (0.878, 0.869) are still ~2-3% under baseline, inside the ~4% noise band but on the low side.
failure_analysis.lesson: An outside-string skip alone does not pay for its extra per-byte guard when 75% of bytes are inside strings; it should only be tried stacked with a faster string-scanning loop, where the outer path becomes a larger share of cost. Benchmark runs with bimodal ratio distributions should be treated as contention-affected.
